records.name: Anecdotal Performance Claims
records.definition: Asserting performance characteristics from anecdote or intuition rather than measured evidence.

records.name: Anecdotal Timing
records.definition: Judging how fast code runs from casual observation instead of controlled measurement.

records.name: Bottlenecks
records.definition: A single stage that constrains overall throughput because all work must pass through it.

records.name: Fixed Provisioning
records.definition: Allocating a static amount of capacity regardless of demand, so the system is either starved or wasteful.

records.name: Fixed-Capacity Design
records.definition: Building a system around a fixed capacity ceiling that cannot grow when load increases.

records.name: Full Materialization
records.definition: Loading an entire dataset into memory at once when streaming or chunking would suffice, risking exhaustion.

records.name: Global Shared State
records.definition: A single mutable state shared across all workers, forcing coordination and preventing independent scaling.

records.name: Guess-Based Capacity
records.definition: Sizing capacity from guesswork rather than a model of arrival and service rates.

records.name: Guess-Based Optimization
records.definition: Optimizing based on assumptions about where time is spent rather than profiling evidence.

records.name: Guesswork
records.definition: Deciding where to optimize by intuition instead of measured profiling data.

records.name: Hard Resource Ceiling
records.definition: A fixed upper bound on a single machine's resources that caps how far vertical scaling can go.

records.name: Inefficient Algorithm Choice

distinctFrom.reason: An inefficient algorithm scales poorly in its own complexity, while an N plus one query issues one extra query per item fetched.

records.definition: Selecting an algorithm whose complexity scales poorly for the expected input size.

records.name: Instance Affinity

distinctFrom.reason: Instance affinity ties a client to one server's state, while temporal coupling requires operations in an undocumented order.

records.definition: Binding a client to a specific server instance for its state, preventing free rebalancing across instances.

records.name: Instance-Local State
records.definition: Holding request-spanning state on one instance, so requests cannot be served by any other instance.

records.name: Local Micro-Optimization
records.definition: Tuning a non-bottleneck section for marginal gains while the constraint that limits performance goes unaddressed.

records.name: Long Blocking Work
records.definition: Performing lengthy synchronous work on a request path, blocking it and inflating latency.

records.name: Origin-Only Serving
records.definition: Serving all content directly from the origin with no edge caching, concentrating load and adding distance latency.

records.name: Premature Optimization
records.definition: Optimizing code before evidence shows it matters, adding complexity for gains that may never be needed.

records.name: Resource Waste/Saturation
records.definition: Running resources far below or far above healthy utilization, either wasting capacity or saturating it.

records.name: Sequential Bottleneck
records.definition: A portion of work that must run serially, capping the speedup that parallelism can achieve.

records.name: Single Monolithic Store
records.definition: Concentrating all data in one store that cannot be partitioned, capping write and storage scalability.

records.name: Single Target Routing
records.definition: Directing all traffic to one target instead of distributing it, wasting capacity and creating a bottleneck.

records.name: Single-Primary Read Contention
records.definition: Serving all reads from the single primary, so read load contends with writes and limits throughput.

records.name: Unbounded Access
records.definition: Permitting callers to make unlimited requests with no rate limit, allowing overload and abuse.

records.name: Unbounded Memory Growth
records.definition: Accumulating state without bound so memory usage grows until the process exhausts it.

records.name: Unbounded Runtime Growth
records.definition: An algorithm whose running time grows without bound as input scales, becoming infeasible at size.

records.name: Arrival and Service Rates
records.definition: The measured rates at which requests arrive and at which a server completes them, the inputs a queuing model needs.

records.name: Bottleneck Awareness
records.definition: The ability to recognize which component limits a system's overall throughput.

records.name: Bottleneck Evidence
records.definition: Measured data identifying which component constrains performance, justifying where to optimize.

records.name: Cacheable Content
records.definition: The requirement that content be stable enough to serve from a cache without harmful staleness.

records.name: Capacity Model
records.definition: A representation of how a system's capacity responds to load, used to predict its limits.

records.name: Complexity Awareness
records.definition: The ability to reason about how an algorithm's cost grows with input size.

records.name: Complexity Model
records.definition: A representation of how an algorithm's resource use scales with input size.

records.name: Externalized State
records.definition: The requirement that session or request state be held outside the serving instance, in a shared store.

records.name: Input Size Model
records.definition: A representation of the input dimension against which an algorithm's running time is measured.

records.name: Invalidation Policy
records.definition: The rules determining when cached entries are considered stale and must be refreshed or evicted.

records.name: Load Model
records.definition: A representation of the expected volume and pattern of demand a system must handle.

records.name: Memory Model
records.definition: A representation of how an algorithm's memory use grows with input size.

records.name: Multiple Targets
records.definition: The precondition that more than one interchangeable backend exists across which traffic can be spread.

records.name: Partition Key
records.definition: The field whose value determines which shard or partition a record belongs to.

records.name: Partition Strategy
records.definition: A scheme for dividing data or work across independent partitions to distribute load and enable parallelism.

records.name: Quota Policy
records.definition: The declared limits on how many requests a caller may make within a time window.

records.name: Repeatable Test Environment
records.definition: A controlled, reproducible environment in which measurements can be compared meaningfully across runs.

records.name: Representative Workload
records.definition: A workload that reflects production usage closely enough that measurements generalize.

records.name: Resource Headroom
records.definition: The degree of spare capacity remaining on a machine before its resource ceiling is reached.

records.name: Space Complexity Awareness
records.definition: The ability to reason about how an algorithm's memory use grows with input size.

records.name: Statelessness or Shared State Strategy
records.definition: A decision to make instances stateless or externalize state to a shared store, so any instance can serve any request.

records.name: Abuse/Overload Protection
records.definition: The ability to shield a system from abusive or excessive request volume.

records.name: Bottleneck Detection
records.definition: The ability to locate the component that most constrains overall performance.

records.name: Capacity Increase without Distribution
records.definition: The ability to raise capacity by enlarging a single machine rather than adding more machines.

records.name: Comparative Analysis
records.definition: The ability to compare algorithms by how their cost grows, independent of hardware.

records.name: Cost Efficiency
records.definition: The degree to which a system delivers its work at the lowest resource cost.

records.name: Dynamic Capacity
records.definition: The ability to add or remove capacity automatically as demand rises and falls.

records.name: Efficient Processing
records.definition: The ability to complete work using the fewest operations and least resource for the input.

records.name: Geographically-Local Delivery
records.definition: The ability to serve content from a location near the user, cutting distance latency.

records.name: Growth Handling
records.definition: The ability to absorb increasing load without redesign.

records.name: Large Dataset Scaling
records.definition: The ability to grow storage and throughput by spreading a dataset across many shards.

records.name: Latency Reduction
records.definition: The ability to lower response time by serving results from a nearer or faster source.

records.name: Load Handling
records.definition: The ability to process a high volume of work without degrading.

records.name: Memory Scalability
records.definition: The ability to handle larger inputs without memory use growing prohibitively.

records.name: Multi-Core Utilization
records.definition: The ability to use multiple processor cores simultaneously for a single workload.

records.name: Origin Offload

distinctFrom.reason: Origin offload relieves the origin server, while local delivery cuts the distance to the user.

records.definition: The ability to relieve the origin server by serving cached copies from the edge.

records.name: Overlapping Work
records.definition: The ability to make progress on multiple tasks over the same period by interleaving them.

records.name: Read Traffic Offload
records.definition: The ability to divert read queries to replicas, relieving the primary.

records.name: Reduced Load
records.definition: The ability to lessen work reaching a backend by serving repeat results from a cache.

records.name: Regression Detection
records.definition: The ability to catch a performance regression by comparing measurements against a baseline.

records.name: Responsiveness
records.definition: The degree to which a system reacts quickly to user actions or requests.

records.name: Scalability Analysis
records.definition: The activity of assessing how a system's cost grows as load or input increases.

records.name: Scale-Out
records.definition: The ability to add capacity by adding more machines that share the load.

records.name: Targeted Improvement
records.definition: The ability to direct optimization effort at the specific constraint that limits performance.

records.name: Traffic Distribution
records.definition: The ability to spread incoming requests across multiple backends evenly.

records.name: Utilization-Based Sizing
records.definition: The ability to size capacity from measured utilization and wait-time targets.

records.name: Wait-Time Prediction

distinctFrom.reason: Wait-time prediction forecasts how long work waits, while utilization-based sizing chooses capacity from measured load and a wait-time target.

records.definition: The ability to predict how long work will wait given arrival and service rates.

records.name: Always-Fresh Reads
records.definition: The degree to which every read returns the most recent write, which caching trades away for speed.

records.name: Cache Invalidation
records.definition: The activity of removing or refreshing cached entries so stale data is not served.

records.name: Constant-Factor Practicality
records.definition: The degree to which constant factors, ignored by asymptotic analysis, affect measured performance.

records.name: Cost/Limit
records.definition: The degree to which a bigger single machine costs disproportionately more and eventually hits a hard limit.

records.name: CPU Cost
records.definition: The degree of processor time a technique consumes, often traded against memory savings.

records.name: Cross-Shard Queries
records.definition: The degree of difficulty and cost of a query that must gather data from multiple shards.

records.name: Distributed Complexity
records.definition: The degree of intricacy introduced by spreading work across distributed nodes.

records.name: Distributed Coordination
records.definition: The degree of coordination overhead required to keep distributed instances consistent.

records.name: Environment Drift
records.definition: The degree to which a test or runtime environment diverges from a reference over time, undermining comparability.

records.name: Implementation Simplicity
records.definition: The degree to which code stays simple and clear, sometimes traded against maximal efficiency.

records.name: Measurement Overhead
records.definition: The degree of performance cost that the act of measuring imposes on the system being measured.

records.name: Model Assumptions
records.definition: The simplifying premises a performance model depends on, which limit how well it matches reality.

records.name: Over-Provisioning
records.definition: The degree to which allocated capacity exceeds demand, trading waste for safety margin.

records.name: Read-Your-Writes Consistency
records.definition: The degree to which a client is guaranteed to see its own prior writes, which replica lag can break.

records.name: Readability/Maintainability
records.definition: The degree to which code stays readable and maintainable, sometimes sacrificed for performance.

records.name: Rebalancing Complexity
records.definition: The degree of difficulty of redistributing data when partitions are added or removed.

records.name: Session Affinity
records.definition: Routing all of a client's requests to the same server instance so its session state stays local.

records.name: State Access Latency
records.definition: The degree of added latency incurred when state is fetched from an external store rather than held locally.

records.name: Throughput/Batching
records.definition: The degree to which batching work raises throughput at the cost of per-item latency.

records.name: Warm-Up Latency
records.definition: The degree of delay before newly-added capacity becomes ready to serve traffic.

records.name: Cache Contract
records.definition: A technique for declaring what a cache entry is keyed by, how long it lives and what invalidates it.

records.name: Context-Keyed Cache
records.definition: A technique for including tenant, identity, version and every input that changes the result in a cache key.

records.name: Cache Invalidation on Write
records.definition: A technique for removing or refreshing cached entries in the same change that writes the data behind them.

records.name: Batch Fetch
records.definition: A technique for loading the related data for many items in one query or call instead of one per item.

records.name: Externalize Session State
records.definition: A technique for moving per-user or per-request state out of instance memory into a shared store.

records.name: Replace Algorithm
records.definition: A technique for swapping an algorithm or data structure for one with better complexity for the inputs at hand.

records.name: Add Index
records.definition: A technique for adding an index on the fields a slow query filters or sorts by.

records.name: Chunked Processing
records.definition: A technique for processing large data in fixed-size pieces, so memory use stays bounded.

records.name: Repeated Stable Computation
records.definition: A defect in which a costly computation or query whose result does not change is repeated on every request.
